title: Learned OCT texture analysis distinguishes sampled brain-metastasis tissue from healthy tissue
summary: A support-vector classifier separated OCT images of sampled brain metastases and healthy brain tissue using histology-derived labels. The analysis retained fourteen tissue samples from a twenty-patient collection. Reported image-level accuracy is exploratory: cross-validation split B-scans, without demonstrated separation of tissue samples or patients, and does not establish surgical diagnostic performance.
ai_technology: Support-vector machines on OCT texture features with PCA dimensionality reduction
organization: Ruhr University Bochum; Technische Hochschule Georg Agricola

evidence.tested: Twenty patients contributed twenty-two tissue samples; histologic purity criteria retained ten tumor and four healthy samples. An experienced neuropathologist assigned tissue-composition reference labels. Texture features from 14,336 OCT B-scans were reduced with PCA and classified using grid-tuned SVMs with tenfold cross-validation. The source reports up to 96.83% image-level discrimination of pooled vital/necrotic tumor versus healthy tissue.
evidence.unknown: B-scans from the same tissue specimen are correlated, and the described allocation does not establish specimen-level or patient-level separation between folds. Normalization/PCA isolation and nested tuning are not established. Purity-selected specimens and small sample counts constrain interpretation; thousands of images do not substitute for independent patients. No intraoperative clinical deployment, margin-level ground truth, recurrence reduction or survival benefit was demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: The SVM combined learned boundaries over multifeature OCT texture measurements to discriminate histology-labeled sampled tissue categories, supplying a specific ex-vivo diagnostic feasibility result. PCA alone is not treated as the enabling AI contribution.

source_review.scope: Read original patient/specimen selection and histology reference, image/texture/PCA/SVM and cross-validation Methods, classification Results and clinical translation limitations. Other laboratory processing details were not independently adjudicated. Source image-level results are explicitly distinguished from unestablished patient-held-out diagnostic accuracy. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
